text:
A most unexpected name sits behind the phenomenon Erling Haaland and the £125m proven marksman Alexander Isak in the Premier League goalscoring chart this season. The rise of Thierno Barry may have surprised even the man himself but stands as a fitting reward for single-minded perseverance and the refusal to quit.
“Fabulous” was David Moyes’s take on Barry’s last performance for Everton, when a double against Coventry took the striker to 10 goals for the season in all competitions and his team temporarily up to fifth. It was high praise indeed from a manager who does not dispense tributes freely, and can appear to be on the French forward’s case constantly, but was no more than Barry deserved for a display that also featured an assist for Everton’s third goal of the night. His six Premier League goals leave him joint third alongside Evanilson of Bournemouth and Aston Villa’s Nicolas Jackson.
“Haaland must be worried about him catching him now,” Moyes said. That line was delivered in jest but also represented a welcome departure from the position Barry found himself in this summer, and from where Everton stood at the close of transfer deadline day.
“I’m stopping, I’m stopping,” says Barry in a searingly honest video released on his YouTube channel in September. Entitled Never Give Up, the episode shows the striker doing exactly that after one miss too many during a private training session with his personal coach. He then breaks down in tears, head in hands in despair, after a dressing down from his lawyer. “Don’t give up, bro,” snaps the lawyer. “Where you come from, you can’t give up.”
Many players in that position would have buried the footage, afraid of broadcasting weakness or of the vicious comments that would invariably follow on social media. Barry told the BBC he spent three weeks worrying whether to post before deciding: “No, I just need to show myself. They need to learn about me because last season I showed a version of me that is not me. And they need to learn about me, how I train hard to be the best on the pitch.”
Barry’s openness was refreshingly well received, even online. In the episode he admits hitting “rock bottom several times last season” when, after a £27m move from Villarreal, he went 16 games without a goal for Everton and failed to register a shot on target until December. He finished his debut campaign in English football with eight goals from 41 appearances, a tally surpassed in 13 matches this season, and was often watching Beto from the bench.
Never Give Up is revealing not only for Barry’s emotional side. It features the striker having private training sessions in England, France and Morocco in the summer. The personal coach, lawyer and personal physio who make an appearance are part of an entourage that also includes a nutritionist and a chef. Barry will not be found wanting in his efforts to establish himself in the Premier League, a process well under way before Everton’s visit to Brentford on Monday night.
“His general all-round play has improved,” says Moyes. “There’s lots of his all-round play that still needs to get better but I’d say his game knowledge, his understanding, has improved. I would never do down any leagues but I think coming to the Premier League from abroad is really difficult in the first year. I think he found it difficult. The expectation on players coming in and being good immediately is built up and he’s needed time to settle.
“He still needs lots of things to make him a rounded centre-forward but there are bits of it that are getting better; he’s beginning to look more clinical. Even in training I’m seeing much better actions than I did last year. Leighton Baines does quite a lot with him, and shows him stuff to make him better, but his integration is much better now too.”
Barry can be a bewildering player capable of inexplicable misses and touches one minute, clinical finishes and creative distribution the next. Everton’s only recognised forward should be closer to Haaland’s tally of 14 club goals for the season. But it is only five years since he started playing as a striker for Sochaux, who he joined after failing in trials as a defender for Clermont and as a central midfielder with Hamilton Academical. Lyon-born, Barry did not come through the academy system in France that could have polished the rough edges. He has had to do it all for himself and, fortunately for Everton given their calamitous end to the transfer window, he has stepped up at the right time.
Moyes, far from just being on Barry’s case, believes the 24-year-old’s story can inspire others. “It should definitely be factored in,” he says of how people should judge a player without an academy background. “Also, not understanding how it works at football clubs and how you go about it. Not in terms of how you behave – he is not a problem in that department – but just how you go about your job and what is expected of you. He is still getting used to it.
“He was in France, then went to Basel [via Beveren in Belgium], then Basel to Villarreal and then Villarreal to here. He also had quite a lot of rejections before he even got out of France, by all accounts. But there is also inspiration behind that. You can show young people that if you put the work in, keep challenging yourself and keep pushing yourself, somebody might just like what they see and pick you up.
“Basel saw something in him and obviously other clubs have decided to go for it as well. We took him as a young, inexperienced centre-forward for £27m, and a year and a half ago it was probably a worse time to be looking for strikers in the market. What ones who were bought at that time have done absolutely brilliantly? Not many. We took a gamble early. Has the gamble paid off? It’s beginning to look better than maybe it did last year but that is because of Thierno’s hard work.”
digest_he: החלוץ הצרפתי של אברטון, תיירנו בארי, הפך לאחת ההפתעות הנעימות בצמרת טבלת כובשי השערים בפרמייר ליג, עם עשרה שערים בכל המסגרות העונה. המאמן דייוויד מויס הביע הערכה רבה ליכולתו ולעבודה הקשה שהשקיע השחקן, במיוחד לאחר תקופת הסתגלות קשה מאוד בעונה שעברה שבה לא כבש במשך ששה עשר משחקים. סרטון תיעודי שפרסם השחקן בעצמו חשף את הרגעים הקשים והתסכול הרב שחווה אשתקד, כולל משברים אישיים ואימוני פרטיים מפרכים. כיום, בזכות התמדה ומעטפת מקצועית צמודה הכוללת מאמנים אישיים, תזונאים ופיזיותרפיסטים, בארי הוכיח את ערכו על המגרש והפך לשחקן משמעותי במערך של אברטון.
